Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Vishmi Gunarathne and Chamari Athapaththu are the two openers for Sri Lanka Women. We will start with some spin as Rameen Shamim has the new ball in her hand. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Sri Lanka Women fight back after Powerplay struggles - Sri Lanka struggled with the ball in the Powerplay, but they came back strongly, picking up wickets in the 7th, 8th and 9th overs to pull things back. With Pakistan at 105/6, they would have liked to restrict them to a lower total, but they just could not get past Fatima Sana, which cost them a few extra runs. Chethana Vimukthi was the pick of the bowlers with a fantastic four-wicket haul, while Malki Madara, Nimasha Meepage and Sugandika Kumari all chipped in with one each. Now, the batters have a strong challenge on their hands, and this is a situation they will most likely find themselves in during the main tournament as well. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Pakistan Women reach respectable total despite collapse - Pakistan Women have finished with a strong total on the board, although given the start they got, they will feel they could have pushed a bit further. The openers were outstanding, racing to 53 in the Powerplay, but once their 60-run stand was broken, the innings lost momentum as they slipped to 105/6. However, skipper Fatima Sana stood tall under pressure, playing a brilliant knock of 37 off 26 with a wide range of strokes, while Aliya Riaz provided excellent support with a crucial 41-run partnership that helped drag Pakistan to a competitive finish and add late momentum.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! The first six overs have belonged to Pakistan Women, and their decision to bat first, so far, is proving to be a good one. Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! The Sri Lanka Women players spread out from the huddle, taking their respective field positions. Muneeba Ali and Gull Feroza are the two openers for Pakistan Women. Mithali Ayodhya has the new ball in hand and is ready to go. Just a bit of a delay, not sure why. Nilakshika Silva is passing a note to the coaching staff, which is rare, as it is more often the other way around. Well, the main issue is that the scoreboard is not up, but it is now, and we are good to go. Let's play...

We can see the Sri Lankan players just outside the ropes, sharing a few chats and giggles among themselves. A few of the bowlers are warming up as well, rolling their arms over. The Pakistan Women batters also look ready, already padded up, and the start of the game is not too far away. Everyone is just waiting for the umpires' go-ahead.

The skipper of Sri Lanka Women - Chamari Athapaththu says that, looking at the conditions, they would have bowled first anyway. Adds that their preparations have also been pretty decent, with playing some good cricket against West Indies and Bangladesh. Shares that they had a two-week camp in Pallekelle, but obviously not conditions like England, so they want to get adjusted and continue their good run of form. Ends by saying that they have a good mix of spinners and seamers and are going into this World Cup with a different composition of squad.

The captain for Pakistan Women - Fatima Sana says that the track looks good, and they want to post a good total on the board and then defend it. Adds that the preparations have been good, with the Ireland series, even though the last couple of games got washed out. Mentions that this is a good opportunity for them to get in some match practice. Ends by saying that their aim is to be in the last four in the World Cup.

TOSS - Pakistan Women have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

A quick recap - While we wait for the toss here, let’s take a look at what happened in the first warm-up game, where Scotland Women, batting first, posted 163/5 on the board after a rain delay pushed the start back by an hour. In response, the Netherlands were bowled out for 105, handing Scotland a convincing 58-run win, and with their recent performances, the Scots are starting to look like real dark horses heading into this World Cup, building momentum at just the right time.

Conditions test awaits Pakistan Women's core - Pakistan, meanwhile, arrive with mixed preparation behind them, with their Ireland tri-nation series heavily affected by rain and yielding inconsistent results against stronger opposition. While they did dominate Zimbabwe earlier in May, the challenge of adapting quickly to English conditions will be key. Much will depend on their experienced core, with Muneeba Ali and Gull Feroza at the top, Fatima Sana leading from the front with the ball, and support from Diana Baig and Nashra Sandhu in the bowling unit. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Sri Lanka Women riding high on confidence - Sri Lanka enter this clash full of confidence after a strong run of results, including a clean sweep over Bangladesh in a recent T20 series and earlier wins against the West Indies. Led by the ever-influential Chamari Athapaththu, they have looked well-balanced and increasingly assured in the shortest format. She will be well supported by Harshitha Samarawickrama in the middle order, while Vishmi Gunaratne adds stability at the top. All-round options like Kavisha Dilhari and Nilakshi Silva give them valuable depth, and the spin threat of Sugandika Kumari adds further control with the ball.

Dress rehearsal begins in England - Welcome to Derby as the countdown to the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026 intensifies, with Sri Lanka Women and Pakistan Women locking horns in an important warm-up fixture at The County Ground. With the tournament set to begin on June 12, both sides will see this as a crucial dress rehearsal to settle combinations, get used to English conditions, and build momentum ahead of the global stage.
